name: PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna Tbk

frontmatter.title: HM Sampoerna - a cash franchise priced for decline
frontmatter.summary: We initiate with a BUY. The market prices HM Sampoerna for permanent revenue decline, yet nine-month 2026 revenue and profit grew inside a flat-tariff regime, the FY2025 tax charge was a one-off and the balance sheet is net cash. A share leader paying out almost all of its earnings at a low multiple is mispriced; the thin free float and the excise cycle keep it there.
thesis: Tobacco excise tariffs have been flat since the 2025 decision, after the ten-percent steps of 2023 and 2024; 2027 is the third consecutive flat year, not a new turn, and the 2026 interim accounts already show revenue and profit growing inside that regime.

Sampoerna is the number one player in hand-rolled, machine-made and smoke-free, with a leading share of the legal market where the volume loss has been driven by illicit trade rather than by share loss.
FY2025 profit was struck at an unusually high tax rate; the normalised rate visible in the 2026 interim accounts lifts earnings without any volume recovery.
The data pack understates depreciation materially; restating it from the audited accounts adds roughly a trillion rupiah a year to the cash-flow base the DCF discounts.
The balance sheet is net cash with no growth capex, so essentially all earnings are distributable and the dividend yield at the current price exceeds our cost of equity.
The risks are real and are in the bear case - a renewed excise cycle, the illicit share, and a free float that the exchange's phased rule forces higher by 2027.

catalysts.event: Final 2027 excise regulation after the DPR consultation confirms a third flat year
Final packaging regulation - plain packaging dropped, graphic warnings widened
FY2026 results - first full year of the flat-tariff regime
First free-float deadline - the minimum rises to twelve and a half per cent
AGMS and the FY2026 dividend declaration

blocks.text: We initiate coverage of PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna at **BUY** with a twelve-month target of **Rp869**, 33.8% above the Rp650 close on 6 November 2026, for a total return of 44.3% once the dividend is included. The stock trades at 9.4x forward earnings and a 10.6% next-twelve-month dividend yield, with net cash and no growth capex [S0].

The variant view is simple: the market is pricing a business in permanent decline, and we think that is one cycle too pessimistic. Our reverse DCF says today's price discounts FY2027E revenue growth of -0.7% every year for ever. Against that, the first nine months of 2026 printed net revenues of IDR87,511.5bn against IDR83,742.9bn a year earlier, and net profit of IDR6,514.9bn against IDR4,511.1bn [S2]. The difference between those two statements is the investment case.
Three things move the value.

First, **the tariff has stopped rising, and the actuals already show what that does**. The government has not raised the tobacco excise tariff since the ten-percent steps of 2023 and 2024, so 2025, 2026 and 2027 are three consecutive flat years; the 2027 decision continues an existing policy rather than turning it [S4]. We therefore give the 2027 decision no incremental credit. What we do credit is the evidence from inside the flat-tariff regime: nine-month 2026 net revenue rose to IDR87,511.5bn against IDR83,742.9bn and net profit rose to IDR6,514.9bn from IDR4,511.1bn, with gross profit of IDR16,016.1bn on that revenue base [S2]. A category that grows revenue with a flat tax is a category where price and mix are working.

Second, **the earnings base is understated by a one-off**. FY2025 net profit of IDR6,609.5bn was struck at an effective tax rate well above both the rate in the first nine months of 2026 and the FY2024 rate, because the company booked additional tax expense through other expenses [S2][S3]. Our FY2026E net profit of IDR8,063.4bn is therefore not a heroic volume recovery; it is mostly the same business taxed normally.

Third, **the cash-flow base in the data pack is wrong**. The pack carries a FY2025 depreciation figure that is a small fraction of the audited charge of IDR1,338.9bn disclosed in the fixed-asset note [S3]. We restate FY2024 and FY2025 from the LK, and the engine rebuilds EBITDA and free cash flow from there: the FY2025 FCFF line in our model is IDR8,609.9bn. This matters for a manufacturer with a large fixed-asset base, and it is part of why our DCF sits above what a screen would suggest.

The risks are not cosmetic. Sampoerna is 92.4% owned by PT Philip Morris Indonesia, and the free float is 7.5% [S0]; that constrains index weights and liquidity, and it is why we accept the lower bound rather than the midpoint of the house cost-of-capital band. The excise hold is a one-year decision that can be reversed, the illicit share of the market is estimated at 13.0% [S5], and the category's legal volume is shrinking. We put all three in the bear case, which values the shares at Rp606, below where they trade today.

Sampoerna is the largest cigarette manufacturer in Indonesia by value and, on its own accounting, the number one player in every segment in which it participates: hand-rolled kretek, machine-made kretek and smoke-free products [S3]. It reports a single operating segment - the manufacture and trading of cigarettes and smoke-free products - so the product split in the revenue note is the only segment disclosure available [S2].

The mix is the business. In the nine months to September 2026, machine-made kretek contributed IDR52,509.2bn of net revenue, hand-rolled kretek IDR25,823.5bn, machine-made white cigarettes a further slice, and smoke-free products IDR1,975.4bn [S2]. Machine-made is growing at a double-digit rate while hand-rolled is shrinking at a similar pace, which is the mechanical consequence of downtrading and of the relative excise treatment of the two classes. Smoke-free is small but growing: volume rose to 1.50 billion units in FY2025 [S3]. The portfolio spans the value end of the market through brands such as Dji Sam Soe Magnum and Sampoerna Kretek, the premium end through Sampoerna A and Marlboro Filter Black, and a heat-not-burn franchise [S0].

The company sells through a national distribution network that reaches traditional retail across the archipelago, and it manufactures in Indonesia with a workforce of 19,326 [S0]. Its competitive advantage is distribution density plus brand equity in a category where the consumer buys a single stick at a time from a warung; that is a real moat, but it is a moat around a shrinking pond, which is why we treat the franchise as a cash cow rather than a compounder.

Ownership is the defining structural fact. PT Philip Morris Indonesia holds 92.4% of the shares and the free float is 7.5% [S0]. Sampoerna is therefore a controlled subsidiary of Philip Morris International rather than an independent listed company: minority holders own a claim on the dividend, not on strategy. Related-party trade is correspondingly large - in FY2025 the company bought IDR8,325.4bn of goods from related parties and sold IDR2,847.8bn to them [S3]. Those purchases are mainly tobacco, flavour and wrapping materials sourced within the PMI network, and they are disclosed as arm's-length with audit-committee oversight [S3].

Indonesia is one of the largest cigarette markets in the world by volume, and the kretek
category - clove-flavoured tobacco - is a local institution with no real export analogue. The
industry is labour-intensive in hand-rolled production and highly mechanised in machine-made,
which is why the mix shift between the two has visible cost consequences. Sampoerna has been
listed since the early nineties and has paid a large share of its earnings out as dividends
for most of that history.

The Indonesian tobacco industry is, for a listed equity investor, a regulated utility with a brand attached. The state sets the excise tariff annually, sets a minimum retail price band, and captures a large share of the retail price; the manufacturer's gross margin is the residual after excise, leaf, wrapping and conversion [S4][S5]. That structure explains why the industry's revenue grows in steps: a tariff increase lifts both revenue and cost of goods, and the net margin effect depends on how much of the increase the consumer absorbs.

The excise history matters more than the 2027 headline. The government raised the cigarette excise tariff by ten percent in 2023 and again in 2024, and has not raised it since: 2025, 2026 and 2027 are three consecutive flat years, with the finance ministry holding the tariff on purchasing-power and industry-continuity grounds and preparing a new administrative layer for illicit product instead [S4]. The 2027 decision is therefore a continuation, not a turn, and we do not treat it as new information. What the flat years have produced is visible in the receipts: state excise revenue fell to about 211tn in 2025 from about 219tn in 2022 even as rates rose, because raising the legal price widens the gap to illicit product and the consumer trades down or across [S5]. The official estimate of the illicit share is about 13.0% of the market [S5].

Enforcement is the part of the policy that is actually tightening, and it is the observable that matters for volume. In the first half of 2026 the customs directorate carried out 8,570 enforcement actions, 3.9% more than a year earlier, seized about 905 million illegal sticks, 95.5% more than a year earlier, and collected IDR72.9bn through the ultimum remedium mechanism [S4]. Seizures rising far faster than the number of actions is the signature of enforcement moving up the chain from retail to distribution. If that rate holds, the illicit share is the one variable in this industry that can fall without a price cut.

Regulation beyond excise has moved in the industry's favour. The draft health ministry regulation that would have required plain packaging has had that provision removed, with the two ministries agreeing instead to raise the graphic health warning to 50.0% of the pack face [S9]. Plain packaging is the measure that would most directly damage brand equity in a category where the pack is the main marketing medium; its removal is a material, if under-reported, positive for the incumbent brand owners.

Industry conditions are stable rather than buoyant. The Ministry of Industry reports that confidence in the tobacco-processing sector was still in expansion in October 2026 but slowing, with new orders and production expanding while the inventory index sits in contraction because warehouse stocks rose - a stock build ahead of the year-end excise transition, not lean management [S8]. There is no evidence of a demand recovery strong enough to lift the category; the point of our view is that the legal market has stopped shrinking, not that it is booming.

Competitive position is strong. Sampoerna held a 30.7% share of the legal market in FY2025, and volume was 79.4 billion sticks - a decline the company attributes to the erosion of legal industry volume by illicit product rather than to share loss [S3]. That share is a share of legal consumption: against an illicit share of about 13.0%, Sampoerna's share of total consumption is roughly a quarter [S3][S5]. It is the number one player in hand-rolled, machine-made and smoke-free [S3]. The competitive set is a handful of large domestic groups plus a long tail of small manufacturers in the lowest excise class; the tail is where illicit and near-illicit product competes, and it is the segment the new excise layer is aimed at [S4].

Five forces, briefly. Rivalry is moderate and concentrated, because excise classes segment the market and the top players compete on brand rather than price. Buyer power is low: the customer is a consumer buying single sticks, and the trade has little leverage over a must-stock brand. Supplier power is moderate in leaf - tobacco is bought from smallholders and traders - and high in one specific sense, because the controlling shareholder is also the principal supplier of flavour and wrapping materials [S3]. New entrants are constrained by excise licensing, distribution and brand spend, but not eliminated: the small-manufacturer tail is the entry channel. Substitutes are the real threat, in the form of illicit product, vaping and heat-not-burn, and the company's own smoke-free franchise is partly a hedge against its cigarette business [S3].

The excise system is tiered by production volume and product class, so a manufacturer's
effective tax rate depends on which tier its brands sit in and on how the government redraws
the tier boundaries. Redrawing them to compress the gap between classes is the standard
policy lever for closing the price gap that illicit product exploits. The industry employs a
large number of workers, directly and through smallholder tobacco farming, which is why
excise decisions are politically as well as fiscally loaded.

The reported history is a flat-to-declining top line with a recovering margin. Revenue was IDR111,211.3bn in FY2022, IDR115,983.4bn in FY2023, IDR117,880.0bn in FY2024 and IDR112,172.0bn in FY2025 [S3]. Gross margin bottomed at 15.7% in FY2024 as excise and leaf costs outran pricing, then recovered to 18.4% in FY2025 on pricing and mix actions [S3]. Operating profit was IDR9,284.0bn and net profit IDR6,609.5bn, or Rp57 per share [S3].

The 2026 interim accounts show the turn more clearly than the annual history. Nine-month revenue was IDR87,511.5bn against IDR83,742.9bn a year earlier, gross profit IDR16,016.1bn, selling expenses IDR5,832.8bn and general and administrative expenses IDR2,490.7bn. Pre-tax profit was IDR8,354.0bn and the tax charge IDR1,839.0bn, leaving net profit of IDR6,514.9bn against IDR4,511.1bn a year earlier [S2]. The year-on-year jump is mostly the tax line: the 2025 comparative was struck at a far higher effective rate because of additional tax expense booked outside the operating lines [S2].

Our forecast anchors on that run-rate. FY2026E revenue is IDR116,771.1bn, representing growth of 4.1%, built from nine-month actuals plus a fourth quarter growing at a slower rate on a tariff-free base [S2]. FY2027E grows 4.0%, which is the 2026 run-rate held rather than improved: 2026 was itself a flat-tariff year, so it is the right base rate for a second one, and no company guidance discloses a further pricing step [S2][S4]. Growth then fades to 2.0% by FY2030E as the legal category's volume decline reasserts against price and mix. Gross margin is held at 18.3%, the nine-month 2026 actual, across the horizon: neither the LK nor the annual report discloses a pricing action after the flat 2026 tariff, so we do not forecast margin expansion [S2][S3]. SG&A is 9.6% of revenue; the effective tax rate is 23.0%; capex is 0.8% of revenue in FY2026E, the FY2025 trough, and 1.2% from FY2027E - at or just above the depreciation charge, because a nominally growing business cannot shrink its asset base for ever - against a company statement that no material capital commitments exist beyond a contractual fixed-asset commitment of IDR300.0bn [S3]. On those inputs, EPS rises from Rp57 to Rp69 and Rp73, and DPS from Rp56 to Rp69 [S0].

Cash conversion is the strongest part of the story, but it is not above one. Free cash flow to the firm was IDR8,609.9bn against EBITDA of IDR10,622.9bn in FY2025, about four-fifths, and IDR6,844.3bn against IDR8,880.0bn in FY2024, about three-quarters [S0]. Capex was only IDR755.4bn in FY2025 [S0], which is why the ratio is high for a manufacturer; the gap to one is cash tax and working capital, not a quality problem. Receivables fell faster than revenue in FY2025 and inventories fell in absolute terms, so there is no channel-stuffing signature [S0].

The balance sheet is in net cash. At end-September 2026 the company held IDR9,124.7bn of cash and cash equivalents against IDR274.0bn of lease liabilities, which are its only debt; the FY2025 accounts show debt at a fraction of equity [S2][S3]. The implied net cash position is what the DCF bridge adds to enterprise value. Working capital is large in absolute terms - IDR11,108.6bn at end-2025 - because the company funds its own excise stamps and leaf inventory, but it is stable relative to revenue [S0]. There is no refinancing risk, no maturity wall and no covenant to monitor.

Capital allocation is a full payout. Dividends paid were IDR6,534.8bn in FY2025 against net profit of IDR6,609.5bn, a payout ratio of 99.1%; the DPS record is Rp55, Rp69, Rp56 and Rp56 over the last four years [S0][S3]. With no growth capex and net cash, there is no plausible alternative use for the cash, and the parent needs the dividend. That is what makes the equity a bond proxy - and why the yield matters more than the growth rate.

Earnings-quality screens are clean apart from two items we flag rather than discount. Related-party purchases of IDR8,325.4bn are the modal channel for value leakage on IDX; they are disclosed as arm's-length and audited, and the audit committee states it has adequate procedures, but a minority holder cannot independently verify the pricing [S3]. Second, the FY2025 tax rate was a one-off, and we normalise it rather than extrapolate it; if the additional tax expense proves recurring, the earnings base is lower than we show [S2].

We value Sampoerna on a DCF of free cash flow to the firm as the primary method (50.0% weight), with the company's own four-year P/E history (25.0%) and dividend-yield history (25.0%) as cross-checks. That set fits this business: it is a single-segment, net-cash, full-payout manufacturer whose value is the cash it distributes, so a cash-flow model with an explicit payout assumption is more informative than a peer multiple in a category where the listed comparables differ in excise class and ownership. The P/E and yield legs are disciplined by using Sampoerna's own trading history rather than an assumed peer premium [S0].

The cost of capital reconciles to the engine. The rupiah risk-free rate is 7.4%; the engine deducts the 1.6% sovereign default spread embedded in that yield and adds our 1.0% judgement premium, so the net risk-free rate in the build is 7.4% less 1.6% plus 1.0%. On top of that it adds a mature-market equity risk premium of 4.2% plus a country risk premium of 2.5% on an unlevered beta of 0.70 (the tobacco industry default) with a debt weight of 0.4%. That gives cost of equity of 11.5% and WACC of 11.5%. Without the judgement premium the build lands a point below the house IDR band of eleven to thirteen per cent on the compounder card; the premium, disclosed here and not buried in the beta, is what brings us to the band's lower bound rather than its midpoint. We accept the lower bound because the free float is thin and the regulatory risk is single-country, and we leave the beta and ERP inputs untouched rather than tuning them.

The DCF produces Rp823 per share. The explicit forecast runs ten years, with free cash flow rising from IDR7,826.2bn to IDR9,377.8bn as revenue compounds and margins hold, and a terminal value at 2.0% growth. The terminal value is 42.8% of enterprise value, so the explicit period carries the majority of the number and the terminal assumption is not doing the work on its own. We add the net cash position from the September 2026 balance sheet, the bulk of it short-term financial assets, and subtract nothing for minorities because there are none [S2].

The card's growth arithmetic is worth stating because it is the test of the terminal value. Growth is manufactured, not declared: g = reinvestment rate x return on incremental invested capital. With capex at 1.2% of revenue against a depreciation charge of 1.2% and operating working capital at 9.9% of revenue, incremental investment is almost entirely the working-capital drag - a fraction of a per cent of revenue a year against a NOPAT margin near seven per cent - so reinvestment is a low single-digit share of NOPAT and the 2.0% terminal growth implies an incremental return on invested capital far above WACC. That is not heroic for a price-led franchise with no capacity requirement: the growth it buys is small and so is the capital it needs. The fade year is FY2030E, when growth reaches its terminal rate and the margin stops moving. The model's rising ROE, from 23.3% in FY2025A to about a third by FY2035E, is a payout artefact rather than improving returns: a payout of 99.0% shrinks book equity mechanically, and we do not capitalise it [S3].

The cross-checks straddle the DCF, and both embed a re-rating that we do not underwrite. The P/E leg gives Rp741 on a 13.0x multiple applied to FY2025 earnings, -9.9% below the primary; the dividend-yield leg gives Rp850 at an 8.1% yield, 3.3% above it. Both multiples are four-year averages of four annual observations, not five, and both sit above today's 11.4x P/E and 8.7% yield, so each leg assumes the stock re-rates toward its own history. That is why they are cross-checks rather than independent confirmations: one is below the DCF and one above, and both rest on a re-rated anchor. We do not argue for a return to the historical double-digit multiple; the legs bound the answer, they do not set it.

The multiple-survival test is the discipline the card requires, and here it cuts both ways. Today the market pays about 6.0x enterprise value to EBITDA. Our terminal value capitalises FY2035E operating profit of IDR12,561.7bn at an exit multiple about a sixth above the entry multiple - the same gap on an operating-profit basis - so part of the target is re-rating rather than cash flow, worth about five and a half per cent of the DCF. We say so plainly rather than dressing it up as a DCF. The justification is that the entry multiple is depressed by two things that are not in the cash flows: a thin free float that the exchange now forces to rise [S10], and an excise scare that the 2026 actuals have begun to answer [S2]. A reader who refuses to underwrite any re-rating should use the bear-case value of Rp606, which is below today's price, or the constant-multiple value, which is the DCF less that re-rating.

Sensitivity is dominated by two inputs: the revenue growth path and the gross margin. The twelve-month value grid below spans four points of revenue growth either side of our path and two points of gross margin either side. Its weakest cell, at four points lower growth and two points lower margin, sits below the current price, so the grid does disclose downside at its edge; it does not test an outright revenue decline, and that case is carried by the bear scenario, which values the shares at Rp606. The WACC and terminal-growth grid shows that a higher WACC alone takes the DCF down by roughly a tenth. The valuation is not robust to any single input; it is robust to the inputs we can source, and the decline case is priced.

What does today's price imply? The reverse DCF solves for the revenue growth rate that makes the DCF equal the Rp650 price: -0.7% a year, for ever. That is a market view of permanent revenue decline, with no credit for the 2026 actuals, the flat tariff, or the smoke-free franchise. We think that is the mispricing.

For a name we describe as a bond proxy, the rate path is the other half of the valuation. The house macro deck has the policy rate at 5.75 through FY2027E, USD/IDR at 18,350 and Indonesian CPI at 3.28: no rate relief, and a currency that keeps imported leaf and wrapping costs drifting up. A yield buyer should price this equity off the long end of the curve, not the policy rate; the spread we require over the policy rate is the equity risk premium plus the country and regulatory premium, which is what the 11.5% cost of capital encodes. The yield leg is the rate-sensitive one: it capitalises the next-twelve- month dividend at the four-year average yield, so each percentage point on the required yield moves that leg by roughly an eighth; a hundred basis points therefore takes it down by about that much, leaving it about a sixth above today's Rp650 [S0], and roughly two and a half points of repricing are needed before the yield leg meets the price. That is why we weight the DCF, not the yield leg, in the target.

The principal risk is policy, and it is binary. The tariff hold is a one-year decision; the government can reverse it in the 2028 budget, and the new administrative layer it is preparing could raise compliance costs or compress the price ladder in ways that hurt the premium brands [S4]. Likelihood: medium in any single year, high over five. Impact: high, because a tariff increase passes through revenue and compresses the margin at the same time. This is the risk that justifies our cost-of-capital premium.

The second risk is the illicit market. At about 13.0% of the market, illicit product sets a price ceiling on legal product and takes the volume that would otherwise absorb a tariff increase [S5]. Enforcement is the swing factor in the 2027 policy: if it fails, the hold buys volume for the illegal trade rather than for Sampoerna. Likelihood: medium. Impact: medium, because it erodes volume slowly rather than at once.

Third, volume and mix. Legal industry volume has been shrinking, and Sampoerna's own volume fell in FY2025 [S3]. The mix shift from hand-rolled to machine-made is good for cost per stick but bad for the premium hand-rolled franchise, where the company is strongest. A faster shift would hit gross margin. Likelihood: high, because it is already happening. Impact: medium.

Fourth, the free float, which is now a dated obligation rather than a permanent discount. With 92.4% held by the parent and 7.5% free float [S0], the stock is excluded from or underweighted in many mandates and the daily traded value is about IDR12.8bn. The exchange has raised the minimum free float to fifteen per cent with a phased transition: issuers with a market capitalisation of at least five trillion rupiah must reach twelve and a half per cent by 31 March 2027 and fifteen per cent by 31 March 2028 [S10]. Sampoerna is in that tier and is not compliant today, so the parent must place roughly five points of the 116,318 million shares - a block close to two-thirds of the current free float - within the next few months. That is a supply event, and it is in the bear case. It is also why we apply no separate liquidity discount in the valuation: the thin float is already priced through the disclosed cost-of-capital premium, and taking it twice would double-count the same fact.

Fifth, related-party dependence. The controlling shareholder is also the main supplier of flavour and wrapping materials, and purchases from related parties were IDR8,325.4bn in FY2025 [S3]. The transactions are disclosed and audited, but a minority holder is price-taker on those terms. Likelihood of a value-damaging change: low. Impact: medium.

Sixth, governance and ESG. Tobacco is a sin sector with a structurally shrinking addressable market in the long run, and the regulator's stated direction - higher graphic warnings, possibly plain packaging in a later cycle - is negative for brand equity [S9]. The mitigants are a clean audit opinion, no pledged assets, and a full dividend record [S3].

The most plausible re-rate for a controlled subsidiary facing a forced float increase is a parent tender offer or a delisting of the minority, and it is not in our probability-weighted target. The route is live: three Indonesian issuers have gone private through controller tender offers in the current cycle, and the free-float rule is one of the stated reasons [S11]. We exclude it because no announcement, filing or statement of intent exists for Sampoerna, and because a tender price would be a negotiated outcome we cannot source; we treat it as optionality on top of the target rather than as a driver of it. The same float increase carries index optionality: the regulator frames the higher threshold as a response to scrutiny from global index providers [S11], so clearing it removes a long-standing barrier to index eligibility and to the demand that comes with it.

Our base case (50.0%) is the model above: the tariff stays flat, revenue grows at the 2026 run-rate and then fades, margins hold, and the shares re-rate partially toward the DCF at Rp834. The bear case (25.0%) is a renewed excise cycle with a rising illicit share, revenue declining outright, gross margin lower and the forced float placement landing on top, which gives Rp606 - below today's price, so the downside is a capital loss, not merely the loss of dividend growth. The bull case (25.0%) is a sustained flat tariff plus enforcement that reclaims illicit volume and a scaling smoke-free franchise, which gives Rp1,204. The scenarios are mirrored on the same three drivers - revenue growth, gross margin and the SG&A ratio - with equal and opposite shocks; the asymmetry in the outcome comes from the starting multiple, not from asymmetric assumptions.

Signposts that would change our view: a 2028 tariff increase above inflation; an illicit share materially above the current official estimate; a market share materially below the current level; a dividend cut or a payout ratio cut; a parent tender offer or delisting announcement; and any sign that the free-float placement is being absorbed without a price concession.

Control sits with PT Philip Morris Indonesia at 92.4%, with a 7.5% free float and 0.2% institutional ownership [S0]. The practical consequence is that minority shareholders cannot influence strategy, board composition or related-party terms; they own a dividend stream. The board is led by a president director and a finance director, with an independent commissioner structure and an audit committee that reviews related-party transactions [S3]. The free float is below the exchange's minimum and must rise on the phased timetable described in section five [S10]; that is a governance fact as much as a liquidity one, because it puts the parent's ownership decision on a clock.

Related-party dealings are large but disclosed. Purchases from related parties were IDR8,325.4bn and sales to related parties IDR2,847.8bn in FY2025, conducted under transfer-pricing methods described in the annual report and reviewed by the audit committee [S3]. There is no disclosed pledge of the controlling stake, and the accounts state that no fixed assets are pledged as collateral [S3]. We found no evidence of share-based dilution: the share count is unchanged at 116,318 million shares, with no buyback, rights issue or employee share plan [S3].

The auditor is KAP Rintis, Jumadi, Rianto & Rekan, a member of the PricewaterhouseCoopers network, and the FY2025 opinion is unqualified - the financial statements are presented fairly in all material respects [S3]. The dividend record is consistent: the company has paid a large majority of earnings every year for at least the last four, and the FY2025 payout was 99.1% [S0][S3]. There is no history of serial rights issues, and the controlling shareholder has not diluted minorities.

ESG exposure is concentrated in the product itself. Tobacco regulation is the industry's existential risk, and the direction of travel - graphic warnings now covering 50.0% of the pack, plain packaging deferred but not dead - is negative [S9]. On the social side, the company's hand-rolled workforce and smallholder leaf suppliers are a material stakeholder group, and the annual report discusses farmer livelihoods and labour practices in the supply chain [S3]. Environmental exposure is modest relative to the sector: the main issues are the agricultural supply chain and energy use in manufacturing, not a large direct emissions footprint.

The dated catalysts are the 2027 excise regulation, expected to be finalised after the DPR consultation in the fourth quarter of 2026 and to confirm a third consecutive flat year [S4]; the final packaging regulation, where plain packaging has been dropped but the graphic warning is being widened [S9]; the FY2026 results in March 2027, the first full year showing the flat-tariff regime [S2]; the first free-float deadline at the end of March 2027 [S10]; the AGMS and dividend declaration in May 2027 [S3]; and the 2028 excise decision in late 2027 [S4].

Between updates we monitor six KPIs. Volume and market share, from the quarterly and annual disclosures, because share loss would invalidate the argument that the problem is the industry rather than the company [S3]. The gross margin, because it is the pass-through gauge for excise and leaf costs [S2]. The SG&A ratio, because a brand war would show up there before it showed up in volume [S2]. The illicit share, from the government's own estimates and from the seizure statistics, because it sets the ceiling on legal volume [S4][S5]. The payout, because the equity case is a dividend case and a cut would be the clearest signal that the parent's cash needs have changed [S3]. And the free float, because the placement is the one dated supply event in the name [S10].

bear.narrative: The tariff hold ends with the 2028 budget and excise rises above inflation while enforcement fails, so the illicit share climbs past 15%, legal industry volume falls mid-single digits and Sampoerna gives back the 2026 pricing gains as it spends to defend the hand-rolled franchise; revenue declines outright. On top of that the exchange phased free-float rule forces the parent to place a large block into a thin float by March 2027, which can take the traded price below intrinsic value.

bull.narrative: The tariff hold runs through 2028 and enforcement starts to bite: in H1 2026 the customs directorate ran 8,570 enforcement actions, up 3.9% yoy, seized about 905m illegal sticks, up 95.5% yoy, and collected Rp72.9bn through ultimum remedium [S4]. If that seizure rate holds, the illicit share falls from about 13% toward 10%, legal industry volume returns to modest growth, and the smoke-free portfolio scales from a small base so price/mix outruns a flat cost base and the payout is sustained.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E +4.1% is built from the actual: nine-month 2026 net revenues were Rp87,511bn against Rp83,743bn (+4.5%), and the fourth quarter of 2025 printed Rp28,429bn; a Q4 2026 at +3% on the excise-free 2026 base gives about Rp116.8tn for the year [S2]. FY2027E +4.0% holds that run-rate: 2026 was itself a flat-tariff year (the government has not raised CHT since the 2023 and 2024 steps of ten percent each), so the 2026 price/mix result is the right base rate for 2027 and the 2027 hold adds nothing incremental [S4][S2]. No company guidance exists for a further pricing step, so none is assumed. FY2028E-FY2030E fade to +2.0% as the legal category's volume decline reasserts against price/mix; terminal growth is 2.0%, below the macro deck's Indonesian CPI path (3.28%) and far below nominal GDP, because legal volume shrinks in real terms and industry excise receipts fell about 1.2% a year from 2022 to 2025 [S5].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: The last two actuals are 18.4% for FY2025 and 15.7% for FY2024; nine-month 2026 came in at 18.3% (gross profit Rp16,016bn on net revenues Rp87,511bn), so the 2025 pricing and mix gains have held rather than reversed [S3][S2]. Neither S2 nor S3 discloses a further pricing action after the flat 2026 tariff, and the 2027 hold is the third consecutive flat-tariff year rather than a new step [S4], so the forecast holds the 9M2026 actual of 18.3% flat for the whole horizon. That is 0.1pp below the FY2025 actual and leaves the margin below its 2019-2021 level because the hand-rolled mix (34% of revenue and shrinking) carries a structurally higher unit cost [S2].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Selling plus general and administrative expenses were 9.5% of net revenues in the nine months to September 2026 (Rp5,833bn + Rp2,491bn on Rp87,511bn) against 10.1% for FY2025, as the company kept brand investment flat while revenue grew [S2][S3]. FY2026E is set at 9.6% to allow a normal fourth-quarter selling step-up, then held at 9.6%: there is no sourced plan for a step-change in brand spend, and a declining-volume category does not support operating leverage, so no further decline is assumed.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The data pack carries D&A of Rp293bn for FY2025, about a fifth of the real charge. The audited LK shows total depreciation of Rp1,338,884m for FY2025 and Rp1,182,777m for FY2024, allocated Rp1,046bn to cost of goods sold, Rp263bn to selling and Rp29bn to G&A [S3, note 7]. The restated facts rebuild history (F1, F2); the forecast holds the FY2025 ratio of 1.19% of revenue flat, because capex is set at or above the depreciation charge from FY2027E so the asset base and the charge stop shrinking.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Cash capex was Rp755bn in FY2025 (0.67% of revenue) after Rp1,827bn in FY2024, and the annual report states there were no material capital-investment commitments in 2025 beyond a Rp0.3tn contractual fixed-asset commitment [S3]. FY2026E is held at the FY2025 trough of 0.8%. From FY2027E capex is set at 1.20% of revenue, at or just above the depreciation charge of 1.19%, because a nominal-growing business cannot shrink its asset base in perpetuity: the FY2023-FY2025 average capex ratio was 1.2%, and holding capex at the D&A ratio is the minimum consistent with flat real capacity [S3].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Operating working capital was 9.9% of revenue in FY2025, down from 10.7% in FY2024 as inventories of leaf and finished goods were run down against a smaller volume base [S3][S0]. Held flat at 9.9%: the company funds its own excise and leaf purchases and there is no sourced plan to change payment terms.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The nine-month 2026 effective rate was 22.0% (tax Rp1,839bn on pre-tax profit Rp8,354bn) and FY2024 printed 23.5%, but FY2025 printed 29.9% because of additional tax expense booked in other expenses [S2][S3]. The forecast uses 23.0%, the sustainable rate implied by the two clean periods, not the FY2025 one-off.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Zero: total debt was Rp343bn at end-2025 against Rp4,775bn of cash, debt/equity is 0.01x, and the company states it finances operations from internal resources [S3]. No borrowing plan is disclosed.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero in forecast. FY2025 other income less other expense was a net Rp176bn cost, driven by FX losses and additional tax expense, and FY2024 was a net benefit; these are non-recurring in nature and are not carried forward [S3].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: No non-controlling interests: the LK shows nil minority interest in profit and equity in every period [S3].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Dividends paid were Rp6,535bn on FY2025 net profit of Rp6,609bn, a 98.9% payout, and the 2023-2025 record is 80-100% of earnings [S3][S0]. The company has net cash and no growth capex, so the forecast holds a 99% payout rather than reverting to the engine's five-year average that includes the 2022 peak cycle.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero: 116,318 million shares issued and fully paid, unchanged in FY2025 and FY2024, with no buyback or rights issue disclosed [S3].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 2.0%, below the macro deck's Indonesian CPI path (3.28% for FY2027E) and far below nominal GDP (real GDP 5.29% plus CPI), so the terminal cash flow is modelled in real decline: legal tobacco volume is shrinking and industry excise receipts fell from about Rp219tn in 2022 to Rp211tn in 2025, roughly 1.2% a year, while the illicit share reached about 13% of consumption [S5]. Price/mix, not volume, carries nominal growth, and the 2027 tariff hold is the third consecutive flat year rather than a new pricing step [S4].

challenges.challenge: The lead driver misreads its own source. S4 says the government stopped raising CHT 'setelah kenaikan masing-masing 10 persen pada 2023 dan 2024' and has held rates 'sejak itu' - so 2025, 2026 and 2027 are all flat and the 2027 freeze is the third consecutive flat year, not the policy turn that 'the excise cycle has paused' describes. The report also claims 'since 2022 the annual tariff increase has been the single largest driver', which S4 contradicts. FY2025 revenue fell 4.8% and 9M2026 rose 4.5%, both in flat-tariff years, so the 2027 freeze adds nothing incremental, yet it is the sole source for FY2027E revenue growth of +3.5% and gross margin of 18.6% (inputs.revenue_growth, inputs.gross_margin) and is repeated in the extreme_call justification.
challenges.answer: Restated the excise history as ten percent rises in 2023 and 2024 and three flat years 2025-2027 [S4]; removed the policy-turn framing from the title, summary, thesis, the investment summary, section two and the extreme_call justification; FY2027E growth now holds the 2026 run-rate instead of crediting the 2027 hold.

challenges.challenge: Capex is below depreciation for the whole forecast and into perpetuity (inputs.capex_pct 0.008 rising to 0.009; inputs.da_pct 0.012 falling to 0.011), so the asset base shrinks about 0.3% of revenue a year while terminal_growth is 3.0%. With payout at 0.99 annual retention is only about Rp82bn, so revenue compounding at 3.5% then 3.0% implies an incremental return on that retention above 300% - card item 1 requires g = reinvestment x ROIIC, stated. No fade is applied either: ROE rises from 23.3% to 34% by FY2035E (model lines roe), against card item 3's fade-to-cost-of-capital default for a franchise the report itself calls a moat around a shrinking pond.
challenges.answer: Capex is now 1.20% of revenue from FY2027E against a depreciation charge held at 1.19%, so the asset base no longer shrinks while revenue compounds [S3]. Added reinvestment rate, implied ROIIC and the FY2030E fade year to section four and to qc_justifications.

challenges.challenge: The cost-of-capital paragraph does not reconcile to model.valuation.coc. The rf actually used is 6.83% (7.45% less default_spread 0.0162, plus the 1.0% premium), not the 7.4% printed; the pre-premium COE is 10.53%, not 11.5%; and the sentence says the mechanical build gives 11.5% and that adding 1.0% lifts cost of equity and WACC to 11.5%, which cannot both be true. 11.5% is also the floor of the card's 11-13% band, not the midpoint (12.0%). fund record coe_premium_note contains the correct arithmetic, so the report text is the defect.
challenges.answer: Cost-of-capital paragraph rebuilt from the engine: risk-free 7.45% less the 1.62pp default spread plus the 1.0pp premium, beta 0.70, ERP 4.23%, CRP 2.46%, giving COE and WACC around 11.5%; the report now calls it the lower bound of the 11-13% band, not the midpoint [S0].

challenges.challenge: Three rendered figures are wrong by a factor of 100 to 1000 because the pctv and money filters expect percent-unit and IDR bn inputs but receive fractions and raw IDR. The summary says 0.1% next-twelve-month dividend yield when model mult.FY2026E.div_yield is 0.1068, i.e. 10.7%, the load-bearing number for the bond-proxy argument. Section 5 says base case (0.5%), bear case (0.2%), bull case (0.2%) for probabilities 0.5/0.25/0.25, so the report reads as a 0.9 total, and says the daily traded value is about IDR12,773,594,984.1bn for mkt.adtv_idr of Rp12.77bn.
challenges.answer: Fixed the three format filters: next-twelve-month yield now renders 10.6%, scenario probabilities render 50/25/25, and the daily traded value renders as IDR12.8bn [S0]. Also fixed the reverse-DCF percentage, which was rendering as a fraction.

challenges.challenge: The sensitivity table cannot disclose downside. All 25 cells of the revenue-growth by gross-margin grid (model.sensitivities[1]) sit above the Rp650 price, the worst being Rp683 at -4pp growth and -2pp margin, so no cell tests a revenue decline at all. The text nevertheless claims that even materially lower growth and a lower gross margin together leave the shares above the current price and that the valuation is robust to any single input - the grid is built so that conclusion is pre-ordained. The WACC grid is fine (955 down to 868 at +1pp).
challenges.answer: Removed the robustness claim and published the actual grid floor: the weakest cell, at four points lower growth and two points lower margin, is below the current price. The grid steps live in the industry config, which analysts may not edit, so the outright revenue-decline test is carried by the bear scenario at Rp606 [S0].

challenges.challenge: The multiple-survival test is asserted, not quantified. Terminal value of Rp129,612bn on FY2035E EBIT of Rp14,085bn is an exit EV/EBIT of 9.2x (8.2x EV/EBITDA) against an entry of 7.2x (6.3x). Holding the entry multiple, the DCF is Rp865, not Rp955: Rp90 per share, 9.5% of the primary value, is pure multiple expansion. The report says part of the return is therefore re-rating but never sizes it, and card item 4 requires the implied exit multiple against the entry to be stated.
challenges.answer: Disclosed that the terminal value capitalises FY2035E operating profit at an exit multiple roughly a tenth above the entry multiple, and that the re-rating is worth under a twentieth of the DCF. Engine arithmetic for the reviewer: exit 8.0x EV/EBIT against 7.2x entry, about Rp31 per share of uplift, constant-multiple DCF Rp791 versus Rp823 [S0].

challenges.challenge: The one dated structural risk is absent. At a 7.5% free float the name is below the 15% minimum, and the registry facts in model.valuation.konglo.profile.free_float require 12.5% by 2027-03-31 (4.7 months away) and 15% by 2028-03-31. That implies a PMI sell-down of roughly 6-8% of the company into a 7.5% float - a supply event the report never mentions, while it repeatedly cites the thin float as the reason for a mid-band cost of capital and a depressed entry multiple.
challenges.answer: Added the exchange free-float rule with both deadlines, twelve and a half per cent by 31 March 2027 and fifteen per cent by 31 March 2028 [S10]; the implied placement is close to two-thirds of the current float and sits in the bear case; reconciled the 0.0 liquidity discount by pricing the thin float once through the cost-of-capital premium.

challenges.challenge: The bear case is far milder than its own narrative. The narrative has legal volume falling mid-single digits and the 2026 pricing gains given back, but the shocks are -3pp revenue growth, -1.5pp gross margin and +0.5pp opex, which leave revenue still rising +1.1% in FY2026E and +0.5% in FY2027E and produce Rp702, which is +8.0% above the current price. The claim that the downside is the loss of the dividend growth, not a capital loss, is therefore an artefact of the shock calibration rather than a finding.
challenges.answer: Bear revenue shock widened from three to six points, so revenue declines outright, mirrored by a six-point bull shock [S4][S5]. The bear value is now below the current price, and the report says the downside is a capital loss rather than only lost dividend growth.

challenges.challenge: The most plausible re-rate for a 92.4% PMI-controlled subsidiary facing a legally forced float increase is a parent tender offer or delisting, and it appears only as a signpost that would change the view, never as a probability-weighted driver. The bull case instead leans on enforcement and smoke-free scaling. Nor is the index treatment that follows a float rise (re-inclusion) mentioned or valued.
challenges.answer: Added the parent tender or delisting route with the free-float deadline and the peer precedents that went private through controller tenders [S11], stated why it is excluded from the probabilities, and noted the index-eligibility optionality the float rise creates.

challenges.challenge: The report's own source holds the strongest bull evidence and it is unused. S4 reports 8,570 enforcement actions in H1-2026 (+3.9% yoy), 905m illegal sticks seized (+95.5% yoy) and Rp72.9bn of ultimum remedium receipts - the enforcement leg of the 2027 policy is already tightening. The bull case is asserted from the freeze rather than evidenced from this data, which is the only observable able to validate reclaiming part of the 13% illicit share.
challenges.answer: The bull narrative now rests on the H1-2026 enforcement data: 8,570 actions, 905m illegal sticks seized up 95.5%, Rp72.9bn of ultimum remedium receipts, tied to an illicit share falling from about 13% toward 10% [S4]. Added facts F40-F44 and the enforcement series to section two and the monitoring list.

challenges.challenge: The claim that cash conversion has been at or above one for three years is contradicted by the two numbers in the same paragraph: FCFF/EBITDA is 0.811 in FY2025 and 0.771 in FY2024 (model lines fcff and ebitda). No ratio is given and no source is cited. This is the paragraph that carries the whole cash-conversion argument and the credibility of the DCF, so the error propagates.
challenges.answer: Restated cash conversion as FCFF over EBITDA of about four-fifths in FY2025 and three-quarters in FY2024, with both numerator and denominator shown for both years, and dropped the unsupported at-or-above-one claim [S0].

challenges.challenge: Unjustified optimism, the mirror of the caution test the card imposes. Gross margin rises to 18.6% in FY2027E and 18.8% from FY2029E (inputs.gross_margin) against the FY2025 actual of 18.38% and the 9M2026 actual of 18.30%, sourced only to S4, which contains nothing on price or mix. Revenue growth of +3.0% for ever from FY2028E sits against the FY2025 actual of -4.8% and legal industry excise receipts of Rp219tn (2022) to Rp211tn (2025), about -1.2% a year per S5. Together these add roughly Rp30-45 per share with no open-market source.
challenges.answer: Gross margin is held at the 18.3% nine-month 2026 actual for the whole horizon and terminal growth is cut to 2.0%, below the CPI path, sourced to the shrinking legal volume and the fall in excise receipts; the 2027 growth rate is the 2026 run-rate, not the tariff hold [S2][S3][S5].

challenges.challenge: S8 is misquoted. The report says inventories contract as producers manage the year-end excise transition; the source says the inventory index is in contraction because warehouse stocks rose (stok di gudang industri meningkat), which is a stock-build warning rather than lean management. Separately, the 30.7% share of the market should be 30.7% of the legal industry (LK p20 and p82), which against a 13% illicit share is about 26.7% of total consumption.
challenges.answer: Corrected the inventory sentence to what the source says, a stock build rather than lean management, and qualified the share as a share of the legal market, about a quarter of total consumption once the illicit share is deducted [S8][S3][S5].

challenges.challenge: The two non-DCF legs are not independent cross-checks and they contradict section 5. Both rest on a four-observation history (own_history pe n=4, mean 13.045; div_yield n=4, mean 0.0808) described three times as five-year, and both assume a re-rating to 13.0x and an 8.08% yield against today's 11.4x FY2025A P/E and 10.7% yield, so half of the Rp878 blend is a re-rating bet - while section 5 states we do not argue for a return to the historical double-digit multiple.
challenges.answer: Called both cross-check legs four-year averages of four observations, disclosed that both embed a re-rating toward the historical multiple, and removed the contradiction with section five by stating explicitly that we do not argue for a return to the double-digit multiple [S0].

challenges.challenge: No engagement with the house macro deck for a name the report itself calls a bond proxy. bi_rate FY2027E is 5.75% and the regime is balance_of_payments_pressure / CAUTIOUS, yet the stock prints a 10.7% yield and one valuation leg is a dividend-yield leg set off a historical average. The report never states whether the required yield tracks the policy rate or the ten-year, which is the first question a yield buyer asks.
challenges.answer: Added a rate paragraph tying the yield and the cost of capital to the house deck path, policy rate 5.75%, USD/IDR 18,350 and CPI 3.28%, and stating that the required yield should track the long end and how much each percentage point moves the yield leg [S0].

challenges.challenge: QC FIX Q1 is still open: valuation.post_bs_review is null in fund record and absent from fund record, so the MOST_LIKELY_BASE_CASE card's required record of what was searched after the 30 Sep 2026 balance-sheet date does not exist.
challenges.answer: Same fix as Q1: valuation.post_bs_review is now written in fund record with its sources, naming every post-30-Sep-2026 item searched and confirming no dividend, asset sale or rights event.

challenges.challenge: QC FIX Q2 is still open: Section 4 says 100bp of long-end repricing takes the Rp850 dividend-yield leg to "about the current price". At DPS 68.63 and a 9.08% required yield that is Rp756, about 16% above the Rp650 price; Rp650 needs roughly 250bp. The sentence understates the move by about Rp106 per share and contradicts the "roughly an eighth" statement beside it.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states the corrected arithmetic: 100bp moves the yield leg by about an eighth and leaves it about a sixth above the current price, and about 250bp is needed to reach it. The contradictory 'about the current price' phrasing is gone.

challenges.challenge: QC FIX Q3 is still open: the multiple-survival paragraph says the exit multiple is "roughly a tenth above" entry and the re-rating "under a twentieth" of the DCF. The figures are 7.04x exit EV/EBITDA vs 6.03x entry, +17% (about a sixth), and Rp46 per share, 5.6% of the Rp823 DCF. The card's mandatory multiple-survival test is understated by about 40%, which makes the DCF look more cash-driven than it is.
challenges.answer: The multiple-survival paragraph now discloses exit at about a sixth above entry and the re-rating at about five and a half per cent of the DCF, replacing 'roughly a tenth' and 'under a twentieth'.

challenges.challenge: QC FIX Q4 is a false positive and the clause should not be deleted: S11 line 31 says the OJK free-float increase is part of the 8-point reform action plan "dalam rangka menanggapi sorotan penyedia indeks global" (in response to scrutiny from global index providers), and S11 lines 54-59 name MSCI. The Section 5 attribution is sourced.
challenges.answer: Verified in the archive before answering: S11 line 31 carries 'dalam rangka menanggapi sorotan penyedia indeks global' and lines 54-58 and 67 name MSCI. The Section 5 attribution to [S11] is supported, so the clause is unchanged and Q4 is closed as a false positive.

missing_bull_case.note: The bull case exists and is properly mirrored (3 shocks: +3pp growth, +1.5pp margin, -0.5pp opex) and names smoke-free scaling and enforcement. It omits the two re-rating triggers specific to a 92.4%-controlled 7.5%-float subsidiary - a parent tender/delisting and the mandated float increase that forces a corporate action - and ignores the H1-2026 enforcement data already in S4.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear narrative (mid-single-digit volume decline, 2026 pricing gains given back) is not matched by its shocks: revenue still grows +1.1% in FY2026E and +0.5% in FY2027E, and the bear value of Rp702 is +8% above the price, so it underwrites no downside. The mandatory free-float sell-down is absent entirely. Credit: likelihood and impact are stated for each of the six risks.

assumption_realism.note: FY2026E is well anchored: revenue +4.1% vs 9M actual +4.5%, EBITDA margin 9.99% vs 9M 9.94%, tax 23.0% vs 22.0% actual and 22% statutory. The D&A restatement is correct and consistently applied (EBITDA = EBIT + D&A; FCFF lifted Rp1,046bn, about 12%). FY2027E +3.5% revenue and 18.6% gross margin rest only on S4, whose own text shows tariffs already flat since 2025.

evidence_and_citations.note: Verified at source: D&A Rp1,338,884m and the 1,046/263/29 allocation (note 7, p342); 30.7% share +0.2pp and 79.4bn sticks -1.8% (p20/p29/p82); 9M2026 P&L and balance sheet (S2); plain packaging removal and 40-50% GHW (S9); FY2025 additional tax from assessments (note 16, p348). Defects: three unit/filter errors, the S8 misquote, the false cash-conversion claim, two archived sources never cited.

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF-FCFF is the right primary for a net-cash 99%-payout manufacturer and the 46.8% TV share is disclosed honestly; own history is the right multiple source under the config. But capex sits below D&A into perpetuity with terminal g 3.0%, there is no fade or ROIIC (card items 1 and 3), the 9.2x versus 7.2x exit multiple is never quantified, and the cost-of-capital paragraph does not reconcile to the engine.

bias_and_tone.note: Candid for a BUY: cross-checks below the DCF are disclosed, re-rating is admitted, the bear value is printed and the reverse DCF is shown. But the sensitivity grid has zero of 25 cells below the current price, so 'robust to any single input' is a construction artefact. Survivability test: doubling the bear probability to 50% still gives Rp874 (+34%), so the rating itself survives.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Terminal g 3.0% is correctly below the deck's nominal GDP path (real 5.29% plus CPI 3.28%), the reporting currency and template match the TOBACCO config, and the excise regime is described in the right terms. Missing: any use of the house bi_rate 5.75% path or the CAUTIOUS regime for a name sold explicitly as a bond proxy.

conservatism_audit.note: Below the last actual or LK rate and sourced: opex 9.6% vs 9.5% 9M; tax 23.0% vs 22.0% 9M and 22% statutory; FY2026E growth 4.1% vs 9M 4.5%; terminal g 3.0% vs CPI 3.28%; payout 99% vs 98.9%. Above and unsourced: gross margin 18.6%/18.8% vs 18.38%/18.30% actual; revenue +3.0% for ever vs -4.8% last actual and -1.2%/yr industry; capex 0.8-0.9% vs D&A 1.1-1.2%. Bear and bull shocks are mirrored, three each, no asymmetry.

calibration.note: qc shows FY2025A EBITDA margin actual 0.0947 vs model 0.0999, gap +0.52pp, and the whole gap is the SG&A ratio stepping from 10.1% to 9.6%, which is the 9M2026 actual (5,833 plus 2,491 on 87,511 = 9.5%); FY2026E EBITDA margin 9.99% vs 9M 9.94%. No drift flag was raised and the only BLOCK flag (extreme_call) is answered with three sources.

signoff.notes: SECTOR VIEW (CONSUMER_NON_CYCLICALS / TOBACCO): BUY on HMSP is the most likely path, not a sector re-rating call. The call is name-specific cash return - 92.4% PMI control, 99% payout, Rp8.9tn net cash, 10.6% NTM yield, share gains to 30.7% of the legal industry - inside a flat-tariff regime the 9M2026 actuals (revenue +4.5%, net profit Rp6,515bn vs Rp4,511bn) have already validated. The 2027 freeze is correctly requalified as the third consecutive flat year, not a policy turn, so the target does not lean on it. Downside is real and priced: the 25% bear at Rp606 sits below the Rp650 price on an outright revenue decline plus the forced float placement, so the BUY is not a one-sided file. TOBACCO stance: selective, not a sector BUY - GGRM remains DISCARD (2026-10-29) and its re-initiation at draft must reconcile to this name-specific logic rather than inherit it. Round-2 closure verified: L1 post_bs_review present in fund record:286 with five sources and an empty bridge; L2 yield leg now Rp756 at 100bp and ~250bp to reach price; L3 exit ~7.04x vs entry 6.03x (about a sixth) and re-rating 5.5% of the Rp823 DCF; L4 confirmed a false positive, S11 offset 2610 and MSCI refs verified, section 5 stands. Target build re-derived independently: 809.3 x 1.1153 - 68.63 = 834.0 base, weighted 0.5/0.25/0.25 = 869.5, TR 44.3% - ties.
